title: Workday Autopilot Agents: What They Do (2026 Guide)
summary: Workday autopilot agents automate work directly within Workday rather than external tools. Understand how this built-in approach differs from alternatives.
body_markdown:
## Learn what Workday's autopilot agents launched


### What Workday announced and when


Mark **October 13, 2026 as the launch date** . The agents are Workday's own, built by the vendor and running inside its platform, not something a customer assembles.


For anyone automating across apps, that makes them one step in a longer chain. The announcement doesn't tell you how that step hands data to the next one, so treat any claim about triggers or outbound connections as unconfirmed until you see them documented.


We couldn't confirm which customers have access now, which editions include the agents, or whether a rollout is staged.


**Don't assume your tenant has them because the launch happened.** Ask your Workday account contact whether they have switched the agents on for you and which modules they cover.


### What the agents do


Workday's newsroom page and its recruiting datasheet describe agents that take over routine tasks in HR, finance and IT.


"Autopilot" here means the agent does the task itself instead of suggesting a next step for a person to carry out. A person sets the work going and reviews the outcome, but the steps in between are the agent's.


The pages we read don't spell out where an agent stops and hands back to a person, so confirm that boundary for each one.


The Deployment Agent, which the next section counts at 5,000 users, is one of these agents. We found no definition of it in the pages we used, so we can't say what it deploys or in which area it works.


Ask Workday what it does before you assume it applies to your process.


### Workday autopilot agents pricing and availability


Whether Workday bundles the agents, meters them or sells them as an add-on, the announcement doesn't say, so we won't guess. Get the commercial terms in writing before you plan a workflow around them.


Look at the Agents screen in[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) for the opposite arrangement. Activepieces connects apps across its 741 integrations, and that screen lists agents your own team defines, each with a plain description of its job, such as a blog enricher and an SEO writer.


On the other side of that line sit Workday's agents, defined by the vendor, which is why the open questions above matter.
